transcript:
Agent: Namaste, kya main Rajesh Sharma se baat kar raha hoon?

Customer: Haan, main hi Rajesh hoon. Aap kaun hain?

Agent: Sir, main Priya bol rahi hoon Fintech Loans ke collections team se. Aapka account hamari system mein overdue dikh raha hai. Aapka March ke liye EMI abhi tak pending hai, sir. Aapke paas 45,000 rupees ka outstanding balance hai.

Customer: Haan, haan, main jaanta hoon. Lekin main abhi payment nahin kar sakta. Mera business thoda slow chal raha hai ek mahine se. Aap kuch aur option deke sakte ho?

Agent: Sir, hum settlement option de sakte hain. Agar aap 32,000 rupees abhi pay kar do, to baaki amount ko hum waive kar denge. Ye aapke liye kaafi achha deal hai.

Customer: <interruption> Thirty-two thousand? Nahi nahi, ye bahut zyada hai. Mera budget mein itna aa nahin sakta. Aur suno, do mahine pehle maine already 18,000 rupees ka settlement kiya tha tumhare sath. Usme mujhe kaha gaya tha ki ye aakhri settlement hoga, aur phir aaplog ko mujhe phone nahin karna. Lekin ab phir se naya balance aur naya settlement? Ye theek nahin hai.

Agent: Sir, wo pehla settlement alag tha. Vo tha March ke liye EMI. Ab jo amount baki hai wo alag account status hai. Hum aapko settlement offer kar rahe hain kyunki—

Customer: <interruption> Nahi, nahi samajhte ho tum. Maine pehle jo settlement kiya tha usme likha tha ki account clear ho jayega. Phir se kyun nayi baat aa rahi hai? Aur 32,000 bahut zyada hai. Main zyada se zyada 15,000 de sakta hoon, abhi baki baad mein.

Agent: Sir, 15,000 bahut kam hai. Hamara manager ne jo offer kiya hai wo 32,000 hai, aur ye final settlement amount hai. Isme interest aur penalties sab included hain.

Customer: Penalties? Main ne kaunsi penalties ka fault kiya? Mere paas to sirf EMI delayed thi. Ye sab charges unnecessary hain. Aur samjho, mujhe internal approval bhi leni hogi apne business partner se paise nikalne se pehle. Kal tak main use call kar dunga. Tab tak main haan ya na nahin bata sakta.

Agent: Sir, theek hai. Lekin aapko ye samajhna chahiye ki ye settlement offer valid hai sirf aaj ke liye. Agar aap kal tak soch lete ho, to offer expire ho jayega.

Customer: Dekho, mujhe ye 32,000 ka offer accept nahin hai. Ye bahut zyada expensive hai. Aur pehla settlement jo maine kiya tha usme iska mention hi nahin tha. Agar aap 20,000 mein settlement kar do, to main soch lunga. Lekin 32,000 mein nahin. Iska mera answer hai.

Agent: Sir, main aapke manager se baat kar dunga aur revised offer ke liye escalate karunga. Lekin aapko ye bhi samajhna chahiye ki jab tak aap settle nahin kar lete, tab tak aapka account legal notice ke under jayega.

Customer: Legal notice? Phir se threat de rahe ho? Dekho, maine tumhe saaf kaha di—32,000 mein main agree nahin kar raha. Agar tum 20,000 mein kar sakte ho to theek hai, nahin to mujhe koi aur option batao. Lekin ye jo offer hai wo accept nahin kar raha main.

Agent: Theek hai sir, main samajh gaya. Main aapke case ko escalate kar dunga senior manager ko. Wo aapko 24 ghante mein callback denge revised offer ke saath.

Customer: Theek hai, par jaldi karo. Aur haan, ek baat aur—mujhe email pe hi communication karna hai aage se. Itne phone calls se mera kaam bhi ruk raha hai. Ye note kar lo.

Agent: Bilkul sir, main ye note kar dunga. Aapka revised offer 24 ghante mein aayega. Shukriya.

Customer: Haan, theek hai.

Agent: Namaste, this is Rajesh calling from Credix Finance. Am I speaking with Priya Sharma?

Customer: Yes, hello. Who is this?

Agent: I'm Rajesh from Credix Finance. Priya, we're calling regarding your personal loan account ending in 4827. Your EMI of 12,500 rupees was due on the 15th of this month, and we see it hasn't been paid yet. Can we discuss this?

Customer: Oh yes, I know about the EMI. I actually tried to pay it three days ago. I have the money, Rajesh, but my bank account is frozen. I cannot make any transaction right now.

Agent: Frozen? What do you mean, Priya? Did you miss some payments to the bank, or <interruption> what happened there?

Customer: No, no, it's not about missing payments. The bank — HDFC Bank — they put a hold on my account. I received a letter saying there was some regulatory compliance check they need to do. KYC review or something like that. They said my account would be unfrozen within a week or ten days, but right now I literally cannot withdraw or transfer any money.

Agent: I see. So you have the funds, but the bank has blocked access temporarily. Okay, that's actually helpful to understand. Do you know what the compliance issue was about?

Customer: Honestly, they were quite vague about it. The letter mentioned something about "suspicious activity flagging" during a routine audit, but I haven't done anything wrong. I think it's just a system error on their end. My husband said these things happen sometimes with large bank transfers for business. He was sending money to a supplier last month, and the bank flagged it. But yes, the bottom line is I cannot access my account right now.

Agent: Right, right. So the funds are there, but the account is locked. When do you expect the bank to unfreeze it? Did they give you a specific date?

Customer: They said within seven to ten working days from when the letter arrived. The letter came on the 20th, so <interruption> that means it should be cleared by around the 29th or 30th of this month. So I'm hoping by early next month at the latest.

Agent: Okay, so we're looking at roughly two to three weeks from now. Priya, in the meantime, do you have any other way to make this payment? Some people use credit cards, or they get a cheque issued from their business account, or sometimes a family member can help with a transfer.

Customer: Hmm, I thought about asking my husband to transfer from his account, but his account is also with HDFC and he's concerned that if there's something flagged on our banking relationship, his might get frozen too. We prefer not to take that risk. And I don't have a credit card with sufficient limit right now. I'm really stuck, Rajesh. This is frustrating because I want to pay, I really do.

Agent: I completely understand, Priya. This is not a situation where you're unwilling — you're blocked by circumstances beyond your control. Let me note this down in your account. Can I confirm your current address so we have it on file?

Customer: Yes, it's 302 Maple Heights, Sector 7, Noida. Same as always.

Agent: Perfect, that's already on file. Now, regarding your EMI — we have 12,500 due for this month. Once your account is unfrozen, will you be able to pay this immediately, or do you need a few days to settle?

Customer: Once it's unfrozen, I'll pay it the same day. I promise you. I have the money sitting there, I just need access back. So it should be done by the end of the month or first few days of next month at the latest.

Agent: Excellent. I'm going to log this as an operational blockage on your account due to a bank-imposed hold. I'll schedule a follow-up call for the 1st of next month to check in with you. By then, your bank should have cleared the hold. Does that work?

Customer: Yes, that's perfect. Thank you for understanding, Rajesh. I was worried you'd think I was trying to avoid payment.

Agent: Not at all, Priya. You've been very transparent about the situation. I'm going to add a note that payment is blocked due to regulatory hold at your bank, not due to any unwillingness on your part. We'll follow up on the 1st. In the meantime, if the bank unfreezes your account earlier, please feel free to reach out and make the payment right away. You have the customer care number?

Customer: Yes, I have it. Thank you. I'll call you as soon as the account is unfrozen if it happens before your follow-up call.

Agent: Perfect. Your account is safe for now, Priya. We're just documenting this operational blockage. Take care, and we'll speak on the 1st.

Customer: Thank you, Rajesh. Appreciate your help.

Agent: You're welcome. Goodbye, Priya.

transcript:
Agent: Namaste, am I speaking with Rajesh Kumar? This is calling from SureFinance Collections. Do you have a moment?

Customer: Haan, haan, I am Rajesh. But listen, I already know why you are calling. I received a notice... a legal notice from your office two weeks back. My wife, she got scared. We don't know what to do.

Agent: Ah, okay. So you received our legal notice. That's good that we're connected now. The notice was issued because your account with us is overdue by 11 months. Your EMI of 18,500 rupees was due on the 15th of every month, and currently you are showing a balance of 2,94,000 rupees outstanding. Can we discuss what happened?

Customer: See, I am not denying anything. The loan is real, the money I took, that was real. But the problem is... <interruption> sorry, sorry, my manager is calling me. One moment.

Agent: No problem, take your time.

Customer: <pause> Okay, I'm back. So the thing is, I lost my job. This happened in April. I was working in the IT company in Bangalore, and they did a retrenchment. Since then I am not getting anything. No salary, nothing. I tried to tell your office before also, but they kept calling and calling. I couldn't pay. What could I do?

Agent: I understand, Rajesh. Job loss is a serious situation. But you see, the legal notice means the matter has moved beyond our collections department. The bank is now considering filing a case against you in court. Before that happens, we want to see if we can resolve this together. Do you want to settle this matter now, or do you want to wait for the court proceedings?

Customer: <voice trembling> Court? No, no, I don't want court. My family will be destroyed. But sir, I also don't have the money right now. I have been looking for a job since April. Only last month I got something — a contract position, but it's only 12,000 per month. How can I pay 18,500 from that? Please, you have to understand.

Agent: I hear you. The fact that you are now employed is a positive step. Tell me, when will you receive your first salary from this new job?

Customer: Next week. The 5th of next month. But sir, I cannot pay the full amount. I have other loans also — a home loan EMI is 22,000, and my wife's personal loan EMI is 8,000. Total is 48,000 every month, and I am earning only 12,000. How can I manage?

Agent: Okay, so you are in a difficult position with multiple obligations. But the legal proceedings have already started, Rajesh. The court will not wait for your salary. What we can do is this — if you can make a payment towards this account within the next few days, even a partial payment, it shows the court that you are making an effort to settle. This can help your case. Can you commit to something?

Customer: <long pause> I... I don't know. Let me be honest with you. I am scared. I don't even know what happens in court. Will they take my house? Will I go to jail? I have heard stories. Please, tell me what I should do. Should I get a lawyer?

Agent: Those are valid questions, Rajesh, and they are important ones. But I am not a legal expert. However, I can tell you this — the best way forward right now is to show the court that you are taking this seriously. A payment, even if it is 25,000 or 30,000 rupees, will demonstrate your intent. Once you make that payment, we can request a pause in the legal proceedings and explore a settlement or a repayment plan with you.

Customer: So you are saying if I pay something, the court case will stop?

Agent: Not immediately. But it will definitely help your case. The legal team will review any payment you make and the circumstances, and they may recommend that the case be withdrawn or suspended. But right now, you are in a position where if you do nothing, the case will proceed. If you take action, there is a chance to avoid that.

Customer: <interruption> Sir, I need to be clear about one thing. I received that notice, and it says I have to appear in court on the 28th of this month. I didn't understand all the words, but my brother-in-law, he read it. He said this is serious. He said maybe I should hire a lawyer to fight this. What do you think?

Agent: The court date is the 28th? That's very soon. Rajesh, I will be honest with you — fighting in court will cost you money for a lawyer, and it may not help your case if the facts are clear that you owe the amount. What will help is if you show that you are willing to settle. This is why I am suggesting you make a payment. Even 50,000 rupees before the 28th would be a strong signal.

Customer: Fifty thousand? <voice breaking> Sir, I don't have that. I have told you, my first salary is next week. And even that, I have to divide between so many bills. My children's school fees are pending. My wife is asking me every day, "What will happen to us?" I am already stressed. I don't know if I can find 50,000.

Agent: I understand. Let me ask this differently. When you get your salary on the 5th, what can you spare for this account? Even if it is 15,000 or 20,000?

Customer: <pause> Maybe 20,000. But only after I pay the home loan and the other urgent things. And sir, even after that, what happens? I still owe so much. Will the bank forgive the rest? Or will this case keep going?

Agent: Those are very good questions, Rajesh. And honestly, they need to be answered by our legal team, not by me. What I am going to do right now is escalate your case to the legal department. I will tell them that you have received the notice, you are aware of the court date on the 28th, and you are expressing a willingness to settle and avoid court proceedings. I will also tell them that you are expecting a salary and may be able to make a payment of 20,000 rupees on the 5th. The legal team will then contact you directly to discuss a settlement structure or a formal payment plan that can be presented to the court.

Customer: So they will call me? How long will it take? The court date is the 28th. That is only... <counts> ... two weeks away.

Agent: Yes, they will call you within the next two to three business days. Please keep your phone available. And Rajesh, one more thing — do not ignore the court notice. If you are required to appear on the 28th, you must appear, or you must have legal representation there. This is important.

Customer: Okay. Okay. So I should not do anything myself? I should wait for your legal team to call?

Agent: Correct. Wait for our legal team. They will guide you on what to do next. In the meantime, if you can confirm that you can make a payment of 20,000 rupees on or shortly after the 5th of next month, that will be very helpful. Can you commit to that?

Customer: <hesitant> Yes. Yes, I think so. After I pay the urgent bills, I will try to keep 20,000 for your bank. But sir, please ask them to call me soon. I am very worried.

Agent: I will make sure they prioritise your case. Thank you for being honest with me, Rajesh. The legal team will be in touch very soon. Take care.

Customer: Thank you, sir. Thank you.

Agent: I understand, sir. I'm calling today regarding your account with us. Your outstanding balance is Rs. 47,500, and your payment was due on the 15th of this month. I wanted to check when you can settle this amount.

Customer: Yes, yes, I know the amount. But do you know how many times I've been called in the last two days? Four times! Four times in one day! I got a call at 8:45 in the morning, then again at 11 AM, then at 3 PM, and yesterday at 7:30 PM. Seven thirty at night! Is this how you people operate? My boss was sitting right next to me when one of these calls came through. Very embarrassing situation.

Agent: Sir, I sincerely apologize for the inconvenience. Let me note this down. So you're saying you received multiple calls outside of—

Customer: <interruption> Outside of permitted hours? Yes! I checked the RBI guidelines myself. You're not supposed to call before 9 AM or after 7 PM. And the frequency... this is harassment. I'm a working professional. I cannot have my phone ringing constantly about money.

Agent: You're absolutely right, sir, and I apologize. These concerns are very valid. Let me escalate this to our compliance team. But before I do that, can we also discuss your payment plan? You mentioned earlier that you would pay. When can we expect the amount?

Customer: That's the other thing. Yes, I said I would pay by the end of this month, but I didn't appreciate the tone the last agent used with me. He was very rude. He said, "Sir, if you don't pay immediately, we will have to take legal action." Like I'm a criminal! I'm not refusing to pay. I'm just asking for a little time. My salary comes on the 28th, and I will pay on the 30th. But the way I'm being treated... it's not right.

Agent: Sir, I'm very sorry to hear that the agent was rude with you. That is completely unacceptable, and I will be documenting this as well. Your feedback is important to us.

Customer: You know what? I'm seriously considering filing a complaint with the RBI. This constant harassment, the calls at wrong times, an agent speaking to me disrespectfully... I could also post about this on social media and let other people know what kind of service you provide. I have a lot of followers, and I don't think your company would want that kind of publicity.

Agent: Sir, I understand your frustration completely. Please don't take that step. Let me assure you that I am personally escalating this matter to our compliance and grievance cell right away. Your concerns about call frequency, timing, and agent behaviour will all be reviewed. Can I at least confirm that you will make the payment of Rs. 47,500 on the 30th as you mentioned?

Customer: Yes, I will pay on the 30th. But I'm warning you — no more calls after this. If I get even one more call before I've made the payment, I will file that RBI complaint immediately. And I mean it. I'm very serious about this.

Agent: Noted, sir. I have documented your commitment to pay Rs. 47,500 on the 30th of this month. I'm also flagging your account for an immediate compliance review regarding call frequency, call timings, and the agent behaviour complaint you've raised. Our compliance team will contact you within 24 hours to address these issues formally. You should not receive any further collection calls until that review is complete. Is there anything else I can help you with today?

Customer: Just make sure this is escalated. Don't let this get buried. And send me something in writing confirming the payment date and that you've stopped calling. I want proof that this has been noted.

Agent: Absolutely, sir. I will send you an SMS and email confirmation of your payment commitment for the 30th, and a separate note confirming that your account has been flagged for a compliance review. You should receive both within the next hour. Thank you for your patience, and I sincerely apologize for the frustration you've experienced.

Customer: Okay. Thank you. I hope this is the last call I get from your team until the 30th.

Agent: Thank you, sir. Take care.

Agent: Hello, am I speaking with Rajesh Kumar?

Customer: Today? No no, not today. Maybe... maybe next week sometime. But I am telling you, I cannot talk right now. <interruption> Can we please just... I will handle it, okay? Just give me some time.

Agent: Rajesh, I need to understand your situation better. Are you facing any difficulty with your income or employment that is preventing you from paying?

Customer: No, no, there is no issue like that. Everything is fine. It is just that... you know, these things take time. I have other expenses also. My daughter's school fees are pending, and there is some repair work at home that I had to do urgently. So the money is a bit tight right now.

Agent: I see. So would you be able to make a partial payment this week? Even Rs 50,000 would help reduce the outstanding amount.

Customer: Partial? Hmm, I... <interruption> Look, I don't know right now. Maybe yes, maybe no. Let me see what happens. Can we just... can we just end this call? I really need to go.

Agent: Rajesh, I need a commitment from you. Can you promise to call me back by Friday with a clear answer on when you can pay?

Customer: Friday? Yes, yes, I will call you. Definitely I will call. But it might be late in the evening or early morning, okay? My schedule is very unpredictable these days.

Agent: Alright, I have made a note. You will call us back by Friday. But Rajesh, just to confirm — can you at least commit to making some payment by the end of next week?

Customer: End of next week? Let me... let me think about it. Maybe. I cannot say right now for sure. Too many things are happening at once. I will let you know when I call you back.

Agent: Rajesh, this is important. The account is already 45 days overdue and if we don't see a commitment or payment soon, we may have to escalate this to our legal team. I want to help you, but I need your cooperation. Can you at least tell me the earliest date you might be able to pay something?

Customer: Legal? No, no, there is no need for all that. I will handle it. I said I will call you back on Friday. Just... just trust me on this. I am a responsible person, I always pay my bills. This is just a temporary situation.

Agent: I understand, Rajesh. I do want to help. But you are avoiding giving me any specific commitment. Can you at least confirm your current contact number is still <noise> 98765-43210?

Customer: Yes, that number is correct. But listen, I really have to go now. My wife is calling me for something. I will definitely call you back. Goodbye.

Agent: Rajesh, wait — can I just get a <interruption>

Customer: <call disconnects abruptly>

Agent: <to system> Call ended. Borrower disconnected. No commitment obtained.

transcript:
Agent: Hello, am I speaking with Mrs. Priya Sharma?

Customer: Haan, yes, this is she. Who is calling?

Agent: Good afternoon, ma'am. This is Vikram from Pinnacle Finance Collections. I'm calling regarding your personal loan account ending in 4827. You have an outstanding EMI of Rs. 12,500 that was due on the 5th of this month. May I have a moment of your time?

Customer: <pause> I... I don't know about any EMI right now. My husband, he usually handles these things, but he... he's been very upset with me lately. <voice becomes quieter> I'm not sure I should be talking about money without him.

Agent: I understand, ma'am. But this account is registered in your name. The EMI for your personal loan taken in August 2022 is now overdue by 16 days. Have you been unable to make the payment, or is there something else going on?

Customer: <interruption> No, no, I know about the loan. It's just... <hesitates> ...my husband, he controls our accounts now. After I had that... that episode last year, he doesn't let me manage things. He says I get confused easily. <nervous laugh> Maybe I do, I don't know anymore.

Agent: I see. Mrs. Sharma, are you in a safe place right now where you can talk? Is your husband at home?

Customer: He's in the next room. He's always... I mean, he likes to know where the money goes. <voice shaky> I want to pay, I really do, but I can't promise anything without telling him first. Last month when I promised payment, I forgot to tell him and then... he got very angry with me. It wasn't good.

Agent: Ma'am, I want to help you. Let me ask — do you have access to your own bank account? Even a separate account?

Customer: <long pause> There's a small savings account my mother opened for me years ago. He doesn't know about it. I have maybe Rs. 8,000 in there, but the EMI is 12,500. And I don't even know if I'm allowed to use that money. <voice trails> He might find out.

Agent: Mrs. Sharma, I'm going to pause our collections conversation for a moment. What you're describing — the control over your finances, the fear of his reaction, not being able to make decisions about your own account — these are serious concerns. Have you spoken to anyone about how you're feeling? A doctor, a counselor, or a trusted family member?

Customer: <quietly> No. I thought it was normal. After I had my breakdown, everyone said he was helping me. But sometimes I feel like I'm not myself anymore. I forget things. I can't remember if I took my medication. <interruption> And now you're calling about money and I don't know what to do.

Agent: Mrs. Sharma, you're doing the right thing by talking about this. I'm going to note your account as requiring specialist support. This is not a standard collections call anymore. What I need you to know is: we are pausing any pressure for immediate payment. Your wellbeing comes first.

Customer: <voice wavers> Really? You're not... you're not angry?

Agent: Not at all, ma'am. I'm going to escalate your account to our empathy team. A trained specialist will contact you within two business days, and they will work with you to find a way forward that keeps you safe. In the meantime, please reach out to the AISA helpline if you need support. The number is 1860-500-5555. They help people in situations like yours.

Customer: <pause> Okay. Thank you. I... I didn't expect that.

Agent: You're welcome, Mrs. Sharma. Your account number is 4827, and I'm flagging this as "Vulnerability - Requires Specialist Care." Please take care of yourself, and we will be in touch very soon.

Customer: Thank you. <call ends>

Agent: Hello, is this Rajesh Kumar? I'm calling from the collections team at MoneyFlow Finance regarding your account.

Customer: No, no, I'm very sure. I have never taken any loan from you people. My name is Rajesh Kumar but there are many Rajesh Kumars in Mumbai. You must have called the wrong Rajesh Kumar.

Because my cousin's friend, he also got a call from MoneyFlow yesterday. He was also saying the same thing — that he never took a loan. Is this some kind of...

Agent: Sir, that's unusual. Can you provide me with his name or the details you remember from that call?

Customer: His name is Vikram Patel. He's from Pune. He got the same kind of call, same amount almost, rupees 12,000 or 13,000 EMI, same collector calling. He also said he never took the loan. And now you're calling me with the exact same story. This is very strange, no?

Agent: <interruption> Sir, I need to understand this better. Are you saying that you and this Vikram Patel both received calls about loans you didn't apply for? And did he also say he never took the loan?

Customer: Yes, yes, exactly. He told me over the phone yesterday. He was very confused also. He said the caller was using his PAN number and everything, but he never applied. And now same thing is happening with me. I'm thinking maybe this is some kind of fraud, no? Maybe someone is using our names and PAN numbers to take loans?

Agent: Sir, I appreciate you sharing this information. This is very serious. Can you confirm — you are absolutely certain you never submitted any application to MoneyFlow, either online or in person, and you have no knowledge of this loan account?

Customer: One hundred percent certain. I have never visited any MoneyFlow office, never applied online, nothing. And my cousin's friend Vikram is also saying the same. We are thinking someone is doing something wrong here. Can you check your records? Maybe someone is using fake documents or something.

Agent: Sir, I'm going to need to escalate this immediately. Before I do, I need to ask you a few verification questions. Can you confirm the address we have on file for you?

Customer: What address do you have?

Agent: Flat 302, Shriram Towers, Bandra, Mumbai 400050.

Customer: No, that's not my address. I live in Andheri, not Bandra. I'm at Flat 15, Green Park Apartments, Andheri West, Mumbai 400058. And I have never lived in Bandra. This proves what I'm saying, no? Someone has used my name and a wrong address to take this loan.

Agent: Sir, this is concerning. I can see there is a significant discrepancy here. Customer: Yes, exactly correct. And I'm worried now. What if my PAN or Aadhar has been stolen? What if there are more loans taken in my name? This is very serious, no?

Agent: Sir, I understand your concern completely. I need to inform you that based on what you've disclosed — the identity mismatch, the address discrepancy, and the pattern you've described with another account holder — I am flagging this account for immediate fraud investigation. transcript:
Agent: Hello, is this Rajesh Kumar speaking?

Customer: Yes, speaking. Who is calling?

Agent: Hi Rajesh, this is Priya from HDFC Lending Collections. I'm calling regarding your personal loan account ending in 4521. Do you have a few minutes to speak with me?

Customer: Ah, yes, the loan. I was expecting your call actually. But listen, I have to tell you something important, okay?

Agent: Of course, please go ahead.

Customer: So the issue is, you see, this loan account... it's a joint account. It's registered under my name and my wife Deepika's name both. And right now, she is out of station. She's in Bangalore for her mother's surgery, and she won't be back for another two weeks at least.

Agent: I understand. So both you and your wife are joint holders on this account?

Customer: Yes, exactly. That's the problem. The bank, when they set up the account, they made it so that both of us need to approve any major transaction. Including payments, you know? It's a joint savings account that's linked to this loan. So I can't just go ahead and make the payment without her signature or approval.

Agent: Okay, I see. So you're willing to make the payment, but you need your wife's authorization first?

Customer: Completely willing, beta. The outstanding amount is around 1,84,000 rupees, right? I want to clear this. But without Deepika's approval, the bank won't process it. She has to be physically present or give written consent, or we need to go together. That's what the bank told us when we opened the account.

Agent: That makes sense. And she's currently unavailable because she's in Bangalore?

Customer: Yes, yes. She's been there for the past week. The surgery was on the 15th, and they said she needs to stay for another 10-12 days for recovery and all. I can't just call her up and ask her to sign something remotely, you know? The bank needs original signatures or an authorized power of attorney document, which we don't have set up right now.

Agent: I completely understand your situation, Rajesh. This is actually quite common with joint accounts. Now, do you have a timeframe for when your wife will be back in town? Or when you might be able to visit the bank together?

Customer: She should be back by... let me see... today is the 22nd, so she should return by the 5th or 6th of next month. Maybe earlier if her mother recovers faster. But we're looking at around 10 to 14 days from now.

Agent: That's helpful. So we can schedule a follow-up call for around the 5th or 6th of next month, once she's back and you both have a chance to visit the bank or authorize the payment together. How does that sound?

Customer: Yes, that works. But I want to be clear — I'm not avoiding this, okay? I'm ready to pay as soon as she's back. It's just this joint account thing that's blocking me right now. It's not my choice, it's the bank's requirement.

Agent: Absolutely, Rajesh, I hear you. And I appreciate you being upfront about this. Let me note down your situation. Your wife Deepika is currently out of station in Bangalore until approximately the 5th or 6th of next month. Once she returns, you'll both visit the bank to authorize the payment of 1,84,000 rupees. Is that correct?

Customer: Yes, that's right. And can you also note that if she comes back earlier, I'll call you immediately and we can arrange the payment sooner.

Agent: Perfect. I'll make a note of that as well. And just to confirm — your current contact number is still 9876543210?

Customer: Yes, that's correct.

Agent: Great. So Rajesh, I'll schedule a callback for you on the 5th of next month. If your wife returns earlier and you're able to make the payment, please don't hesitate to reach out to us. You can also initiate the payment directly through your bank's portal once you have her authorization.

Customer: Sure, I'll do that. Thanks for understanding, Priya.

Agent: Thank you for your honesty and cooperation, Rajesh. We'll speak again on the 5th. Have a good day.
